text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Conservative party leader Wolfgang Schuessel wants to depoliticise Austria's banks as a result of the suicide of Kontrollbank's chief executive Gerhard Praschak, who blamed party influence in the banking sector for his suicide.
- Gerhard Randa, chief executive of Bank Austria, sees postal savings bank PSK and Bawag bank as major competitors in the banking sector in the future.
- Rating agency Moody's rates Bawag's deposit ratings at Aa3/Prime-1.
- Carinthian state leader, conservative Christof Zernatto, says Austria should lay all party politics aside and join NATO as quickly as possible.

- Austria and Germany's largest state Bavaria will join forces in border control when Austria joins the EU's Schengen agreement in October. Vienna airport invested 370 million schillings to make Austria's major airport Schengen-compatible.

- Chamber of Labour and labour unions said at their traditional Labour Day meetings that they want to fight shareholder value-policies and have a more active industry in a bid to fight "turbo-capitalism".
- Contructer Bau Holding will take over the building unit of Germany's Moll AG, while Moll AG will in return receive a share in Bau Holding.
DIE PRESSE
- The public prosecutor's office will investigate the affair around Gerhard Praschak's suicide. Meanwhile the opposition parties demand the privatisation of all banks.
- OeIAG, the government's privatisation agency, should become a holding for all state-owned companies to secure the future of Austria's industry, the Chamber of Labour and labour unions demand.
- OMV finally seems to have chosen Marc Hall to become its fifth chief executive to replace Wolfgang Ruttensdorfer who was appointed state secretary in the finance ministry.
- Gerhard Randa chief executive of Bank Austria, which took over the majority stake in Creditanstalt at the beginning of the year, plans to merge all foreign business of the two banks.
- Austria reported a trade deficit of 2.8 billion schillings for January and February 1997 continuing a trend from the previous year.

- Fibremaker Lenzing plans to cut $15 million in spending for its Indonesian subsidiary. Its loss-making U.S. unit will not receive any further contributions from its parent as it expects further losses in 1997.
KURIER

- Insurer Wiener Staedtische plans to sell its contracts through postal savings bank PSK should it take over the government's stake. The insurance company also plans to raise its stake in Bank Austria.
OOe NACHRICHTEN
- The Social Democrats are coming under growing pressure to privatise Bank Austria, which is ruled by the City of Vienna, where the Social Democrats have had a majority for the last fifty years.
